practiceReport.name: Seth McGowan
practiceReport.archetypeNote: Perimeter speed/cut position (RB) — requires full deceleration/burst clearance on lower-body tags (76% Questionable baseline).
factors: Officially ruled Out on weekly game status report
practiceReport.beatComment: McGowan went down with the injury while returning a kickoff in the first half of the Week 11 loss. The rookie seventh-round pick had been solidified as the top backup to starting running back Jonathan Taylor, but DJ Giddens now is positioned to serve as Taylor's main understudy for however long McGowan is sidelined. McGowan can be safely ruled out for the Week 12 game against the Giants, though a Week 13 bye could help the 25-year-old back avoid additional absences beyond that.

practiceReport.name: Drew Ogletree
practiceReport.archetypeNote: Standard NFL positional availability baseline (78% Questionable conversion).
practiceReport.beatComment: For the third time in four weeks, Ogletree failed to draw a look in the passing game, but he wasn't held off the stat sheet entirely, as he collected a pair of tackles on special teams. Though the fifth-year tight end has been active for all 11 of the Colts' games, he's cobbled together a lowly 4-21-0 receiving line on seven targets.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Akeem Davis-Gaither
irAndReserveTracker.byeWeekNote: Week 13 Bye excluded from NFL 4-game minimum count
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Davis-Gaither was already ruled out for Sunday's game against Miami in what would be his second consecutive missed contest due to a knee injury. Now that he's been placed on IR, the seventh-year pro will be required to miss at least four games, so his next chance to play is Week 15 against the Titans on Sunday, Dec. 20.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Mo Alie-Cox
irAndReserveTracker.byeWeekNote: Week 13 Bye excluded from NFL 4-game minimum count
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Alie-Cox was already ruled out for Sunday's game against the Dolphins, and his groin injury is severe enough for him to warrant a stint on injured reserve. That means he'll be required to miss at least four games, and with the Colts on a bye for Week 13, that means the next time Alie-Cox can play is Week 15 against the Titans on Sunday, Dec. 20. Will Mallory (hamstring) has also been ruled out for Week 10, so Drew Ogletree and Pharaoh Brown will serve as the Colts' backup tight ends behind Tyler Warren against Miami.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Jaylon Carlies
irAndReserveTracker.byeWeekNote: Week 13 Bye excluded from NFL 4-game minimum count
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Carlies hurt his neck in Week 9 against Dallas and didn't practice at all last week before being ruled out for Sunday's win over the Dolphins. Now that he's landed on IR, the third-year linebacker will need to miss at least the Colts' next four games. Austin Ajiake and West Weeks will likely soak up the rotational defensive snaps that Carlies had been getting.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Alec Pierce
irAndReserveTracker.byeWeekNote: Week 13 Bye excluded from NFL 4-game minimum count
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Additionally, Pierce acknowledged that playing in Week 1 was a bit lofty, per Bowen, with the WR saying Wednesday that he was still managing some pain at that stage. In any case, Pierce indicated that he's confident that his current recovery plan will lead to a full return to health. When that will be remains to be seen, but the 2022 second-rounder is still on IR ahead of Week 12, with the Colts presumably not planning to rush him back, given the team's 3-8 record in a campaign that's been marked by the team moving several key players ahead of the trade deadline.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Cam Taylor-Britt
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Taylor-Britt suffered the injury on the first play of the fourth quarter of Sunday's 16-10 loss to the Vikings. It's another blow to the Colts' secondary, given that the team was without Sauce Gardner (calf) during Sunday's game, and fellow defensive back Justin Walley sustained a knee injury during the contest. Taylor-Britt will be required to miss at least the next four games, so the earliest he can return is Week 12 against the Giants on Sunday, Nov. 29. Kenneth Harris and Kapena Gushiken are both in line for more defensive snaps in the absence of Taylor-Britt.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Micheal Clemons
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Clemons sustained a toe injury in the team's 33-30 overtime loss against Kansas City on Sunday night, and he will now be forced to miss at least four contests while recovering. His absence won't have a major impact on the team's defensive approach.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Caden Curry
irAndReserveTracker.byeWeekNote: Season-ending IR — ineligible to return in 2026
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: In a corresponding move, Indianapolis signed veteran defensive end Carl Lawson from its practice squad to its 53-man roster. Over the first 11 weeks of the regular season, Curry recorded 26 tackles (14 solo) including 1.0 sacks and two fumble recoveries on defense, but most of his snaps came on special teams. He'll have to miss at least the next four games as he recovers.

irAndReserveTracker.name: D.J. Montgomery
irAndReserveTracker.byeWeekNote: Season-ending IR — ineligible to return in 2026
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Montgomery signed with the team in early August, ultimately reeling in two of three targets for 21 yards during the preseason. The wide receiver appears to have picked up an abdominal injury at some point during the preseason, and he is now set to miss the entire 2026 campaign while on IR, unless he reaches an injury settlement with Indianapolis.
